records.region: Northern and eastern Victoria Island, Arctic Canada: western headward lakes, Zeta Lake, a northern lake passage and an eastward river to Norway Bay.
records.candidate_name_role: no_supported_representative_river_name; named lake component retained separately
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: The two original maps establish the selected geography and a named lake component but provide no supported representative river name for the whole route. The lake and receiving-bay labels remain limited to their respective roles.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The chosen route begins among small lakes west of Zeta Lake, turns southeast and east through connected waters, bends north through a longer lake and river approach, and enters Zeta Lake. It crosses the shared map boundary within the lake country, continues north through a broad lake passage, turns east through its outlet and adjoining channels, and follows the lower river around a southern bend before reaching Norway Bay. It is east of the separate Nanook and Hadley Bay drainages. The Washburn Lake publication title is not a name for this selected corridor.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded geographic and naming-scope reading of all 34 chosen constituent sublines against two already retained original 1:250,000 land-resource maps. Separate original windows account for the initial lake opening, short lake-to-lake and stream joins, southern turn, northward lake/channel approach, Zeta Lake passage and shared sheet boundary, northern lake passage and eastward outlet, middle river and tributary joins, lower southern bend, final eastward channel and actual Norway Bay terminal. No material unseen geographic interval remains at ordinary corridor scale. The remaining uncertainty concerns a representative river name, not missing cartographic correspondence or exact modeled bank positions.
records.supported_name_scope: Zeta Lake is directly labeled on the selected inland lake passage, on both adjoining original maps. Norway Bay is the labeled receiving coastal water. Neither name establishes a representative name for the entire selected river-and-lake corridor.

scope_limits: The direct Zeta Lake labels are retained as a lake-component finding even though the whole river-system name remains unresolved.
Norway Bay is receiving-water context. It and the Washburn Lake sheet title are not promoted to river names.
No neighboring Nanook River or Hadley Bay identity is transferred to this distinct eastward drainage.
Historical cartographic silence does not establish absence of a current local or official river name.
The original maps establish ordinary corridor geography, not current year-round flow, a surveyed river length, exact banks, every branch name or legal name boundaries.

bounded_name_observations.name: Zeta Lake
bounded_name_observations.role: Directly mapped selected lake component only; no supported whole river-group name.

bounded_name_observations.name: Norway Bay
bounded_name_observations.role: Receiving coastal water only, not a river name.

records.region: Southern Arizona, United States, and northwestern Sonora, Mexico; San Cristobal Wash–eastern Pinacate–Puerto Peñasco coastal setting.
records.candidate_name_role: Supported natural component only; no representative whole-system name established.
records.material_pending_reason: The eastern Arizona approach and westward departure from San Cristobal Wash into the southbound border corridor remain unestablished. The lower selected westward passage across the dune/plain setting to its actual Gulf coast ending is also not shown as a connected selected waterway. These actual through-link gaps are one material-pending feature, despite a supported named natural reach.
records.geographic_disambiguation: San Cristobal Wash is a supported selected natural reach in Arizona. The named A. Sonoyta lies on a separately mapped southern course; regional Sonoyta basin membership, the nearby municipality and neighboring watercourse labels do not identify the entire selected feature.
records.completion_scope: The bounded three-original research pass is complete as an activity. Whole-feature geographic/name correspondence remains materially incomplete; this is not a completed naming-scope hold.
records.supported_name_scope: A selected northern Arizona reach follows the directly labeled San Cristobal Wash corridor north and northeast of Sheep Mountain. The name is not assigned to the full selected object.

component_scope_limits: The supported natural reach name is preserved independently of whole-object uncertainty.
This is ordinary geographic correspondence, not an exact-bank, vertex, surveyed-source or current-flow requirement.
Absence of a demonstrated map connection is not a claim that local or episodic drainage cannot occur.
No current shoreline, surface flow, discharge or waterbody-operation claim is made.

bounded_name_observations.name: San Cristobal Wash
bounded_name_observations.role: Supported Arizona natural reach only; the earlier opening, later border/plain transfers and selected western coastal passage remain unestablished.

records.region: Western Ungava, Nunavik, Québec: selected lake/stream corridor in and beyond the southern Peters study setting.
records.candidate_name_role: No river name is established for the actual selected route from the primary originals inspected. Rivière au Chien Rouge is a discovery lead for the terminal vicinity only, not a researched candidate assignment or whole-group name.
records.material_pending_reason: The selected western opening, upper excursion, successive lake/stream connections, southern dip and eastern terminal are not established by sufficiently readable primary cartography. This is one material-pending feature with no whole-route candidate.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The separate Buron, Saint-Fond and Feuilles regional labels are not transferred to this selection. Rivière au Chien Rouge remains an unconfirmed terminal-vicinity discovery lead only.
records.completion_scope: The bounded source pass is finished, but neither retained CEHQ cartography nor the actually read simplified Peters figures establish the chosen complete route. The unavailable companion is excluded.

scope_limits: No actual headwater or initial source-lake name established.
Actual chosen lake entries/exits, intermediate joins and lower terminal correspondence remain unestablished.
A discovery lead near the terminal is not proof of a representative identity for the whole synthetic group.
No present-flow claim, precise bank, exact mouth vertex or single name for every selected fragment is asserted.

unverified_discovery_leads.name: Rivière au Chien Rouge
unverified_discovery_leads.scope: Discovery context only; no assigned reach or whole-system candidate.

records.region: Southern Pacific Costa Rica: Río Blanco and General valley, the lower Coto Brus junction, Río Térraba and its northern estuarine network.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative receiving-river system identity only. The selected group includes a Río Blanco upper approach, mapped upper connecting reaches, Río General, lower Río Térraba and northern estuarine channels, plus two separately assessed fragments of lower Río Coto Brus. These are not one scalar hydronym.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected upper Blanco branch, inland General and lower Térraba are distinct named reaches. Both selected Coto Brus tributary fragments remain separately identified. The actual endpoint lies in the northern estuarine network toward Isla Viuda and the Boca Nueva–Boca Brava sector, not Boca Coronado or a certified open-ocean mouth.
records.completion_scope: All five selected fragments, the selected upper opening, main inland joins, both tributary fragments and their joining sequence, the lower estuarine continuation and the actual selected endpoint were compared with readable original cartography at ordinary regional/corridor scale. This is completed bounded representative-system research, not exact bank/vertex matching, formal name registration, current flow verification, or certification of a single natural river from one source to an ocean mouth.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative receiving-river system identity only. The selected group includes a Río Blanco upper approach, mapped upper connecting reaches, Río General, lower Río Térraba and northern estuarine channels, plus two separately assessed fragments of lower Río Coto Brus. These are not one scalar hydronym.

scope_limits: Río Grande de Térraba is a bounded representative-system candidate, not a name for every selected reach or either tributary fragment.
The upper source map supports Río Blanco and the continuous connecting network but does not label every upper reach; no exact Blanco–Chirripó–General transition is certified.

The stored terminal lies in the northern estuarine channel network toward Boca Nueva–Boca Brava. Its exact local channel name and ocean-mouth identity are not established or needed for this bounded representative-system finding.
The cartography and estuarine study are historical, generalized sources; they establish geographic/name correspondence, not current water extent, flow, salinity or dam operation.
The optional original-source failures are preserved as access/availability details and do not create a second primary pending status.

bounded_name_observations.name: Río Blanco
bounded_name_observations.role: Clearly mapped upper branch only; exact intervening reach-name transitions unasserted.

bounded_name_observations.name: Río Coto Brus
bounded_name_observations.role: Both separately assessed selected tributary fragments through their General confluence.

bounded_name_observations.name: Río Térraba / Río Grande de Térraba
bounded_name_observations.role: Supported lower receiving river and representative system identity; exact final estero name and ocean-mouth identity remain unasserted.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
